record.original_question: What infrastructure should a distributed community use so that interactions among communities, sub-communities, individual members, and people outside the community can be integrated into the shared context while remaining transparent to each participant despite differences in devices, device capabilities, location, and information structure?

evidence.quote: Another important aspect of community management is the interactions that are possible that must be integrated into the context, whether facilitated by the context or developed outside the context. These interactions can be between communities (or sub-communities), between the community as a whole, between individuals in the community, or with individuals outside any community. Different interactions can have different purposes that are best served by alternate communication styles; they may be collaborative, informational, or social. At the level of an individual in the community, the mechanisms used for the interactions should be transparent. The individual should not be concerned with the devices or capabilities of devices, or with the location or structure of the information in the interaction.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a distributed community modeled as a collection of participants partitioned into (possibly nested) sub-communities, together with a set of external individuals who do not belong to any sub-community. Interactions may occur (i) between two communities or sub-communities, (ii) within a community as a whole, (iii) between two individual members of a community, or (iv) between a member and an external individual. Interactions may serve collaborative, informational, or social purposes, and each participant accesses them through a device with possibly differing capabilities, from possibly differing physical locations, and possibly differing local representations of the shared information.

Design a unifying communication infrastructure for such a distributed community that satisfies the following requirements simultaneously:
1. Every interaction of types (i)–(iv), whether mediated by the shared context or initiated outside it, can be incorporated into a single coherent shared context maintained by the community.
2. From the standpoint of any individual participant, the infrastructure is transparent: the participant need not be aware of the particular device or device capabilities used by other participants, of the geographic location of any participant or resource, or of the underlying structural representation of the information being exchanged.
3. The infrastructure supports different communication styles appropriate to the purpose of each interaction (collaborative, informational, or social).

Specify the components, abstractions, and guarantees of such an infrastructure, and justify that the three requirements above hold.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is a high-level open design problem about infrastructure for distributed communities, not a precisely formulated mathematical conjecture. No specific definitive solution appears in the literature; related work on groupware, federated systems, and ubiquitous computing addresses pieces of the problem but no comprehensive accepted answer is documented.

status_evidence.snippet: Listed as an open problem regarding integrated, transparent interaction infrastructure for distributed communities.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is posed as open, with no resolution indicated.
